analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the event. כְּבוֹא אַבְרָם מִצְרָיְמָה gives its timing, “when Abram entered Egypt,” and וַיִּרְאוּ הַמִּצְרִים states what happened, “the Egyptians saw.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces the short Qal wayyiqtol form יְהִי, third person masculine singular, used impersonally.

analysis.evidence: In כְּבוֹא אַבְרָם מִצְרָיְמָה, the directional ending on מִצְרָיְמָה marks Egypt as Abram’s destination. His entry into Egypt sets the time when the Egyptians saw the woman.
analysis.morphology: The preposition כְּ introduces a temporal clause with the Qal infinitive construct בוֹא. Abram is its subject.
